title: Hierarchical and longitudinal models
text: Structured random effects describe serial correlation within subjects: ar1(0 + time | id): first order autoregressive factor times; cs(0 + time | id), homcs(): compound symmetry; diag(), homdiag(), us(): diagonal unstructured; ou(t | id), exp(t | id), gau(t | id), matern32(t | id): continuous time (Ornstein Uhlenbeck) spatial kernels numeric times coordinates. equally spaced times two models coincide (rho = exp(-1 / range)), AIC values agree; OU form also handles irregular times. TMB engine uses automatic differentiation much faster large multilevel models; gives estimates default engine.
code: Tn <- 6; N <- 40 long <- data.frame(id = factor(rep(1:N, each = Tn)), time = factor(rep(1:Tn, N)),                    t = rep(1:Tn, N), x = rnorm(N * Tn)) e <- unlist(lapply(1:N, function(i) as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.6), Tn, sd = 0.8)))) long$y <- 1 + 0.5 * long$x + e + rnorm(N * Tn, 0, 0.3) f_ar1 <- regcomp(y ~ x + ar1(0 + time | id), family = "normal", data = long, engine = "tmb") f_ou <- regcomp(y ~ x + ou(t | id), family = "normal", data = long, engine = "tmb") c(ar1 = AIC(f_ar1), ou = AIC(f_ou)) #>      ar1       ou  #> 665.8609 665.8609

"log_f": log F(m, m) prior penalty P = -sum(m/2 beta - m log(1 + exp(beta))) (Greenland Mansournia 2015).
